# Disclaimer & Operational Notice

> **Important**: PocketDSO is a development and diagnostic tool designed strictly for **hobbyist, educational, and experimental use**. Please read this disclaimer carefully before using or building this project.

---

### 1. Not for Critical or Safety-Related Decisions
* PocketDSO must **never** be used for mission-critical, life-support, medical, automotive safety, industrial compliance, or high-voltage / mains monitoring applications.
* Do not rely on the measurements, waveform captures, frequency estimates, or telemetry generated by PocketDSO for critical engineering, certification, or safety-critical decisions.

### 2. Hardware-Dependent Accuracy & Inherent Physical Limitations
* **Physical Hardware Limits**: All calculated metrics—including DC voltage levels, true AC RMS ripple, peak-to-peak amplitude ($V_{\text{pp}}$), signal frequency, and FFT spectrum analyses—are inherently bounded by the physical hardware.
* **ADC Resolution & Non-Linearity**: The ESP32-C6 SAR ADC has known non-linearities, quantization limits, and noise characteristics. Software filtering and calibration routines can condition the signal, but software **cannot** overcome or fix hardware noise floors, component tolerances, or physical ADC limits.
* **Component Precision**: The accuracy of your readings depends directly on the components you use. Resistor divider tolerances (e.g., standard 5% carbon vs. 1% metal-film), thermal drift, contact resistance on breadboards, jumper wire inductance, and breadboard parasitic capacitance directly impact the measured voltages and high-frequency response.
* **Probe Impedance & Loading**: Without an active high-impedance buffer, passive resistive divider networks load high-impedance signal sources, which can alter the circuit behavior under test.

### 3. Electrical Safety & Maximum Voltage Ratings
* **Pin Overvoltage Hazards**: The raw ESP32-C6 GPIO input pins accept a maximum voltage of **$0\text{ V}$ to $3.3\text{ V}$**.
* **Negative Voltages**: The inputs **cannot** tolerate negative voltages ($< 0\text{ V}$). Connecting negative or alternating signals with negative swing directly without DC biasing will damage the microcontroller.
* **Mains Electricity Warning**: **NEVER** connect PocketDSO to 110V/230V AC mains electricity or any high-voltage circuits. Doing so risks fatal electric shock, fire, and catastrophic destruction of the development board and any connected host PC or USB power source.
* **Common Ground Precautions**: When powered via a PC USB cable, the ESP32 ground is tied to your computer's chassis ground. Connecting the probe ground clip to a non-isolated or floating voltage potential can short-circuit your computer's USB port.
